newsitem.title: USA: Abercrombie & Fitch IPO set to make a splash.
newsitem.headline: Abercrombie & Fitch IPO set to make a splash.

text.p: Casual wear retailer Abercrombie & Fitch Co., renowned for its rugged, outdoor wear since 1892, makes its highly anticipated stock market debut this week.

The strength of Abercrombie's casual wear brand and its consistent earnings growth have made it one of the jewels in the Limited Inc.'s $7.9 billion retail empire, and investors are likely to snap up its stock at its debut.
"This is hot, hot, hot," said John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket newsletter.

Abercrombie, which outfitted the safaris of Teddy Roosevelt, Ernest Hemingway and the expeditions of Admiral Byrd to the North and South Poles, has been repositioning itself since 1992 to appeal to a more youthful, fashion-conscious audience.
Abercrombie's established name, the success of other niche retail IPOs, and a resurgent enthusiasm for IPOs should combine to make the 7 million share deal a coveted one.

Shares of the Reynoldsville, Ohio-based company are expected to make their debut later this week at an estimated price range of $14 to $16 per share. Lead underwriter Goldman, Sachs is offering the shares.
Analysts expect the stock to immediately move above its offering price. Fitzgibbon said growing demand for the deal means it could outstrip initial expectations of a $2 to $3 premium at the opening.

The Limited bought Abercrombie & Fitch from Oshman's Sporting Goods Inc. in 1988. In recent years, Abercrombie has outperformed most of the Limited's other units including Limited Express and Limited Too. After the IPO, Limited will hold about 95 percent of Abercrombie's voting power.
Abercrombie's prospects look promising, say analysts.

"The company should be able to continue its excellent growth record," said Mark Basham, new issues analyst at Standard & Poor's. "We expect earnings growth to equal or exceed 30 percent over the next four years."
Abercromnie reported 1995 sales of $235.7 million, up 42 percent from 1994 sales of $165.5 million.
Its same store sales, or sales from stores open at least a year, rose 5 percent in the soft retail market of 1995, while same store sales for the Limited fell 2 percent.

The IPO is expected to outshine that of Abercrombie's sister unit, Intimate Brands Inc., last year. The parent of Victoria's Secret, went public in October and has risen only about 10 percent from its initial price of $17.
Basham said he sees Abercrombie's clothes as "having a broad appeal. And they are expanding the product line -- that will bring more people in the store."
